answerEvidence.summary: This key is not incorrect: A and B both need fresh Pod initialization, while C already has the updated ordinary-volume file and rereads it without replacing any existing C Pod. Alternate context: A/B Pods predate the update, their environment/subPath modes are unchanged, and every protected C Pod continues reading its already refreshed ordinary projected file as specified. Evidence: The source separates environment and subPath nonrefreshing consumers from ordinary updating volumes. The stem independently supplies C current file, application reread and an explicit no-restart/no-replacement rule.

distractorEvidence.summary: Refreshing only A leaves B current pre-update Pods with their old subPath projection, so not all three applications receive the updated configuration. Alternate context: B still uses subPath but its existing Pods are already post-update replacements with current configuration, C is already current, and only A remains stale. Evidence: The freshly reread ConfigMap unit excludes subPath from automatic refresh and initializes new Pod configuration from the source. The alternate context changes prior freshness, not B consumption mode.

Refreshing only B leaves A current pre-update Pods consuming the old process-start environment, which cannot receive this update by waiting. Alternate context: A retains environment-at-startup consumption but its existing Pods already obtained current values through an earlier post-update replacement, so only B now needs new Pods and C is current. Evidence: The source initializes environment values when Pods start and says existing ConfigMap environment variables do not automatically update. The alternate case preserves that exact contract.

A full new-Pod rollout could refresh configuration but replaces C existing Pods, directly violating the written restriction regardless of application availability. Alternate context: Replacement is allowed for all three Deployments and all are intentionally reinitialized from current configuration, for example when every application reads configuration only on startup. Evidence: New Pods initialize configuration from the ConfigMap. No source claim that all rolling updates cause downtime is needed: the actual v4 prohibition is replacement of existing C Pods themselves.

rubric.notes: 46/48, independently scored for this v4 hash. Actual source rules plus explicit current-state and C-Pod preservation premises support technical critical fours. Literal a/b countercontexts preserve their consumption modes and vary prior replacement state, giving distractorEvidence four. Difficulty three records lower-edge Advanced with strongly supplied observations; clarity three records the long setup and easy full-rollout exclusion. Full c033 concerns initial kind/name/key wiring, not refresh lifecycle, and this remains the same r-c013 fact rather than another counted encounter.
